narrative: The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job, so it recommends denying the promotion. This is not a judgment about your ability; it reflects a pattern in which your current profile looks more like employees who exit than those who stay. The strongest influence is your overall experience of 6–10 years, which pushes the prediction toward leaving. Although many employees who stay have 1–5 years of experience, your longer track record is associated with greater mobility. The second strongest factor is your 1–5 years in your current organization, which also pushes toward leaving; this is common among stayers, but in your case it adds to the exit signal. The third strongest factor is that you report other job opportunities, which strongly raises the leaving prediction—only about 23% of employees predicted to stay report such opportunities. Other details, such as not feeling you received the promotion you deserved, low job satisfaction, no bonus, no medical insurance, and feeling psychologically exhausted, reinforce this picture. Before denying the promotion, consider discussing your career path, recognition, and retention risks. You may want to clarify your intent to stay and what support would make the role worth remaining for.
